title: OpenHW CV32E40S
_note: The CORE-V CV32E40S: the SECURITY variant of the 4-stage RV32 core -- the
cv32e40x pipeline plus PMP / Smepmp, machine and user mode, hardened CSRs
with shadow copies, dummy-instruction and PC-hardening countermeasures, and
the integrity-checked OBI interfaces.  Its own cv32e40s_manifest.flist is the
closure: rtl/include/cv32e40s_pkg.sv and every rtl/*.sv.
Unlike cv32e40x, which needs ONE bhv file, this family needs THREE, and the
extra two are not simulation scaffolding: cv32e40s_csr instantiates
`cv32e40s_sffs` and `cv32e40s_sffr` for every hardened CSR's rdata and shadow
register, and the only definitions of those two modules in the repository are
bhv/cv32e40s_sim_sffs.sv and bhv/cv32e40s_sim_sffr.sv (the vendor expects a
technology cell there).  Without them cv32e40s_csr and everything above it
has an undefined child.  bhv/cv32e40s_sim_clock_gate.sv is the third, used by
the sleep unit and the CSRs.
Not rows: the RVFI tracer and its OBI shims, cv32e40s_core_log and
cv32e40s_dbg_helper (simulation-only), the sva/ assertion modules bound into
the core, and the wrapper that binds them; the three bhv modules are sources
but excluded as rows by `^cv32e40s_sim_` (they are stand-ins for library
cells, exactly like OpenE906's pa_f_spsram_* models).
First local sweep 2026-10-28: 48 rows, 42 comparable, **36 proven**, 48 / 48
with 0 undriven, 39 co-sim PASS, **0 `read_uhdm`-only co-sim divergences**.
Surelog acb31e60 (#4229) was already in the tree, so this variant elaborated
42 / 42 on the FIRST attempt -- cv32e40x lost six rows to that segfault,
including its core, on the same `'{default: PMA_R_DEFAULT}` declaration.
SIX rows have no reference because read_slang cannot read them, and Verilator
splits them 4 / 2 -- measured per row, never carried over from cv32e40x,
BECAUSE THE SPLIT IS NOT THE SAME ONE:
| row | Verilator | read_slang |
| controller | clean | `'obi_inst_req_t' cannot be used in an expression` |
| controller_fsm | clean | same |
| if_stage | clean | same |
| instr_obi_interface | clean | same |
| data_obi_interface | REJECTS `Member 'wdata' not found` | `no member named 'wdata' in 'REQ_TYPE'` |
| load_store_unit | REJECTS `Member 'wdata' not found` | same |
On cv32e40x the same two groups hold DIFFERENT modules: there controller and
controller_fsm are the ones Verilator rejects, and data_obi_interface and
load_store_unit are the ones it lints clean.  The security variant's default
type parameters are not the plain variant's, so a classification copied
across the two would have been wrong in four places.  Measure each family.
What DID generalise, over 13 measured rows across both variants, is the
DIAGNOSTIC: `'<type>' cannot be used in an expression` is read_slang's own
limit (Verilator lints those clean every time), while `no member named X in
'<TYPE>'` means the member really is absent at the module's defaults and
every tool agrees.  Useful for cv32e41p and core-v-mcu, but it is an
observation to re-check, not a law.
Open leads: THREE formal-only `differs` -- cs_registers (co-sim diverges on
BOTH readers, so shared), core (no co-sim: escaped interface ports) and
sequencer -- plus 3 SAT-budget rows (ex_stage, whose co-sim divergence is
also shared, mult and register_file_wrapper).  sequencer and core each carry
4 never-assigned source nets, the shape that folds a miter trigger to a
constant, so dump the optimised miter before calling either ours.
